text: The rwb-source-data slice of RWB-E2-022 owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC12 sit on RWB-P6-E2022-APP, RWB-P7-E2022-APP and RWB-P4-E2022-APP, and the cross-service proof on RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG. This story is written with six new criteria that test only its four deliverables - the contact-point read, the failed-count operation, the message append and the fold.
why: The Work Package gives an empty screen list for this story and the split plan makes the message path of rwb-comms the primary slice of the key; an APP story that owned a legacy criterion would have to prove a send it does not build.
read: Work Package B2-P1-016 story line (acs empty, tcs_legacy TC-E2-022-01 to -14, secondary true); legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 4 and 7; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7
applied_in: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria; 16 Test cases; 19 Out of scope
confirm: The rwb-comms and rwb-source-data service owners
impact: If a legacy criterion is later moved here, it keeps its legacy wording and its test case and this story gains a copy of it; nothing is lost from the legacy key.

text: The two new operations are fixed as GET /contact-points and POST /contact-points/{contactPointKey}/failed-contacts on base /api/recovery/source-data/v1, with RFC 9457 problem bodies and the status set 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; the ledger extension is POST /interactions and GET /interactions of RWB-P1-E1066-APP carried with the message fields. The 404 of an unknown contact point carries the problem title "Contact point not found".
why: No source gives these operations a path, a status set or a problem title, and the legacy interface was an in-process method; the contract of the caller cannot be built against nothing.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-022 section 12 (the published interfaces); TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 (no such operation); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13; legacy section 14 for the message IDs reused
applied_in: 5 Exception paths X2; 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 12.1; 14 Validation and messages
confirm: TechX API owner and the rwb-comms service owner
impact: A different path or status set changes the OpenAPI fragment and the WireMock mappings of RWB-P6-E2022-CON, not the acceptance criteria.

text: The answer renders consent_given true as GIVEN, false with a consent_at as WITHDRAWN, and no extension row as UNKNOWN, and carries dataAsOf as the business date of the DP02 freshness stamp of the party's ACE customer row, because no contact view carries a date.
why: TSD P1 T3.5 states the three states as data (a missing row is unknown, false with a date is withdrawn) but names no rendering, and the legacy criteria assert the strings GIVEN and WITHDRAWN; v_ace_contact has nine fields and none of them is a business date.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.5 (consent_given and consent_at); TSD P1 v3 T3.4 v_ace_contact fields DF-ACE-075 to DF-ACE-083; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP02 DAILY, expected by 08:00; legacy AC1, AC2 and AC5
applied_in: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 3; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 11 Data
confirm: Data steward (RW-DATASTEW) and the rwb-comms service owner
impact: A different rendering changes the answer schema and the caller's conduct check, not the stored row.

text: A contact point read as MOBILE is a v_ace_contact row of contact_type PHONE whose usage_code is a mobile usage, and one read as LINE is the PHONE row the party uses for LINE OA; the token of a contact point is contact_type:key of the ACE row and it is the only identifier any answer carries.
why: contact_point_ext.contact_type is restricted to PHONE, EMAIL and ADDRESS and v_ace_contact has no LINE branch, while the legacy criteria speak of MOBILE and LINE contact points; the token is the key both tables and the ledger share.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.5 (PHONE, EMAIL, ADDRESS check constraint) and T3.4 (contact_key as contact_type + ':' + key, usage_code from ACE phone.contact_usage); legacy AC1, AC2 and the legacy guardrail that the phone number stays a token
applied_in: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 2; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC6; 11 Data; 13 Configuration
impact: If ACE exposes a LINE contact type in RWB-ACE-001, the mapping loses one branch and the answer gains a value; the token format is unchanged.

text: The delivery result of a message is a second append with the same external_ref and never an update, because the ledger of RWB-P1-E1066-APP is append-only and has no update path; delivery_status and external_ref are added to interaction with ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and the index ix_interaction_external_ref, and whichever of the two slices of RWB-E2-022 merges second adds nothing.
why: The legacy code updated the ledger entry to Delivered, Read or Failed, the target table has an append-only trigger and no application update path, and the same two columns are needed by the letter slice of the same key in the same wave.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-022 section 9 (the delivery values) and section 12 (InteractionLedgerApi.updateDelivery); RWB-P1-E1066-APP BR4 and its append-only trigger tr_interaction_append_only; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-18
applied_in: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3; 12.7; 13 Migration; 19 Out of scope
confirm: The rwb-source-data service owner and the rwb-source-data DB owner
impact: A mutable delivery status would need the trigger removed and the append-only rule of the ledger qualified; the two columns stay the same.

text: The failed count of a contact point rises by one per (contact point, reference) and a repeat of the same Idempotency-Key answers the stored count without a second raise; the retry limit of 5 stays with the outbox sender JOB-11 of rwb-comms and is not counted here.
why: The FSD calls failed_count a consecutive count of failed attempts while the legacy criterion raises it on one failure, and no source state whether a redelivered result raises it again; without a rule the count rises on every replay.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-022 AC8 and AC9 and section 12 (the retry limit 5, assumed, DL11); FSD P1 v3 A2.1.3.2 (failed_count, consecutive failed attempts); TSD P1 v3 T3.5 DF-EXT-018; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09
applied_in: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 8; 8 Business rules BR6 and BR9; 13 Configuration
confirm: Conduct and QA officer (RW-CONDUCT) and the rwb-comms service owner
impact: A different rule changes when the count resets; it changes no column and no path.

text: The channel and delivery values are read through the reference-data client library of DP-07 with a local fixture until the rwb-case reference-data contract lists them, because TSD P1 T3.8 lists no LOV-CHANNEL for P1 and no delivery-status list at all.
why: The answers need two closed value sets and this service owns neither; LOV-CHANNEL left P1 with the objects that used it, and no list in TSD P1 carries SENT, DELIVERED, READ or FAILED.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.8 (the P1 list inventory and the list of lists that leave P1); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 9 and section 12 (NSS and LINE OA result maps)
applied_in: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules BR1; 12.2; 13 Configuration; 19 Out of scope
confirm: Data steward (RW-DATASTEW) and the rwb-case reference-data owner
impact: If rwb-case declines the lists, their values must be versioned reference rows in this schema, which is new work on the per-service sequence.
